h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ל״ג Pesach — Maamar Lamed Gimmel

p: "Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem"
only for being one who feared Him,
that you are one who fears God, etc.'
For he did not perform the mitzvos under compulsion,
And this is according to what they said
(יְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק ט' הֲלָכָה ה', הוּבָא בַּתּוֹסָפוֹת סוֹטָה כ"ב:):
"Love, so that if you come to hate,
know that one who loves does not hate;
be one who fears, so that if you come to rebel,
know that one who fears does not rebel."
For fear is effective in conquering the evil inclination,
"May the fear of Heaven be upon you
like the fear of flesh and blood";
And at the beginning of Shulchan Aruch Orach Chaim:
that the King of kings stands over him,
fear will immediately come to him.
And this one conquers his inclination under compulsion.
Now Avraham Avinu's attribute is love,
and from this came out the dross of Yishmael,
And Yitzchak, whose attribute is "the Fear of Yitzchak,"
from him came out the dross of Esav,
And this is what is said:
"Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem,"
and nevertheless "in His commandments he greatly desires,"
that he not perform the mitzvos under compulsion,
like a servant who serves his king out of fear,
And as for what they said in the Midrash,
that Avraham was not called "one who fears God"
we explained it according to what they said
in the name of our holy Rebbe of Rimanov,
that they could not do anything
against the will of Hashem, may He be blessed;
and here, since it was not truly
רְצוֹן ה' יִתְבָּרֵךְ לִשְׁחוֹט אֶת יִצְחָק,
the will of Hashem, may He be blessed, to slaughter Yitzchak,
לֹא רָצָה יָדוֹ לִיקַּח אֶת הַמַּאֲכֶלֶת,
his hand did not want to take the knife,
עַד שֶׁשְּׁלָחָהּ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
until Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, sent it forth
And all this was because Avraham Avinu
אוּלַי זֹאת הוּא מִצַּד נְגִיעַת עַצְמוֹ,
lest this be from his own personal interest,
And therefore at the Akeidah he was clarified
And akin to this we find in the Gemara
regarding Rabbah, to whom someone repaid a debt in the Shemittah year,
that the mitzvah was not yet complete,
Rabbah would have been happy at fulfilling the mitzvah.
"His seed will be mighty in the land":
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה,
for through this he merited that his bed was complete,
that even among his seed no dross was found;
and "the lip of truth will be established forever."
"The generation of the upright will be blessed":
שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ אַחַר כָּךְ לְיַישֵּׁר הַלֵּב כְּסִיל,
for afterward they will merit to straighten the foolish heart,
And even though the righteous are for light,
And after Yaakov Avinu was born,
Avraham and Yitzchak too were called Israel
for their bed too was complete,
for Yishmael and Esav are not reckoned as their seed,
"In Yitzchak shall seed be called to you" —
Shin is the secret of the three Avos,
for they merit the three holinesses of the Avos;
they merit the holiness of Yaakov Avinu,

paragraphs.text: Midrash Shocher Tov, Tehillim 112:1 — "'Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem': This is what Scripture says, 'Grace is false and beauty is vain'… How much Avraham did before the Holy One, yet he was praised only for fearing Him, as it says, 'For now I know that you fear God.'… And why is he 'fortunate'? Because he did not perform the mitzvos under compulsion (angarya), but with joy."

paragraphs.text: Yerushalmi Berachos 9:5 — "Act out of love and act out of fear. Act out of love: for if you come to hate, know that you love, and one who loves does not hate. Act out of fear: for if you come to rebel, know that you fear, and one who fears does not rebel." Tosafos, Sotah 22b (s.v. Parush me'ahavah), quotes this Yerushalmi word for word.

paragraphs.text: Berachos 28b — Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai blessed his students: "May it be His will that the fear of Heaven be upon you like the fear of flesh and blood." His students said: "Only that much?" He said: "Would that it were! Know that when a person sins, he says, 'Let no one see me.'" Rashi: "Would that" — if it were so, you would refrain from many sins.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Mikeitz 1 — “In all the deeds of the Akeidah Avraham Avinu’s limbs acted on their own out of great alacrity, except for taking the knife, which was not His will; therefore his hands did not want to take it. But Avraham Avinu suspected himself that perhaps this came from the incitement and laziness of the evil inclination, and therefore it is written ‘he sent forth his hand,’ with force. And so too here it is written ‘lest he send forth his hand’: with force, not with the desire of the heart, but through the incitement of the serpent.” Connection: The same Rimanov reading of the Akeidah; there Avraham suspects the yetzer’s laziness rather than love of his son, and the forced “sending forth of the hand” is turned to Adam reaching for the Tree of Life without the heart.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Menachem Recanati, Recanati on the Torah, Vayera — “‘For now I know that you fear God’: we know that Avraham was a lover, so why was he not praised for his great quality of Chesed, but only for fear? Know that fear is of two kinds. Outer fear is below love: fear of transgressing the king's command lest one be punished. Inner fear comes when a person grasps the Creator's greatness and dreads lest, in his own deficiency, some flaw be found in him that would send him out of the King's palace. He fears out of the abundance of his love; this is the fear above love, and of it is said ‘you fear God.’” Connection: Recanati asks the same question, why the man of love is praised only for fear at the Akeidah, and answers with an inner fear born of love, dread of being found flawed, which Rav Tzadok specifies as fear that the deed might stem from self-interest.

paragraphs.text: Gittin 37b — Rabbah was owed money by Abba bar Marsa, who brought it in the Shemittah year. Rabbah said, "I release it"; he took the money back and left. Abaye found Rabbah sad… "Did you tell him, 'Even so'?"… Rashi: Rabbah said, "This scholar had no sense from the start, for he should have said, 'Even so.'"

paragraphs.text: Ta'anis 15a — Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: "Not all is for light, and not all is for joy. The righteous are for light and the upright are for joy: 'Light is sown for the righteous, and for the upright of heart, joy' (Tehillim 97:11)." Rashi: the upright are for joy, for the upright are greater than the righteous.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 63:3 — "Avram was called Avraham; Yitzchak was called Avraham… Yaakov was called Yisrael… Yitzchak was called Yisrael, as it says, 'These are the names of the sons of Yisrael who came to Egypt with Yaakov'; Avraham was called Yisrael."

paragraphs.text: Nedarim 31a — "But there is Yishmael [who is Avraham's seed]! — It is written, 'For in Yitzchak shall seed be called to you.' But there is Esav! — 'In Yitzchak,' and not all of Yitzchak." Rashi: Esav is not called the seed of Yitzchak.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 204a (Vayakhel) — "What is Shabbos?… When this point rises and the light shines, she is crowned with the Avos; and once crowned with the Avos she joins and unites with them to be one, and all is called Shabbos: Shabbos is Shin–Bas. The Shin is the secret of the three Avos, who unite with the only daughter (bas), and she is crowned with them."
